Markets & Liquidity

Thin Fiat Books Crack as Kraken’s Loonie Market Drops to C$24,250

Kraken’s Canadian-dollar order book plunged to C$24,250 on Saturday morning while the U.S. dollar book held $57,700, underscoring a week in which gold, equities, and bitcoin fell together.

From dispatches by Roger, The Bitcoin Zodiac, M.W., and Jeff Booth

At 3:00 a.m. Eastern on Saturday, Kraken’s isolated Canadian-dollar order book abruptly lost its bids, sending bitcoin down to C$24,250—roughly $17,000 U.S. at the prevailing exchange rate—across 976 trades while the exchange’s U.S. dollar book quoted $57,700 for the same coin [s552]. Roughly 244.8 BTC changed hands on the Canadian book between 06:30 and 09:45 UTC before recovering above C$79,000 by five o’clock and C$87,700 by Monday [s552]. Kraken support stated there was no breach and that executed trades stand [s552].

The two prices differed by sixty percent because a price is not a property of an asset. It is a promise made by whoever is standing on the other side of your trade.

Quoting Adam Back’s terse diagnosis that the USDCAD market maker ran out of money, Roger noted that the Bitcoin ledger itself never missed a block [s552]. By 09:05 UTC on Monday, November 23, bitcoin traded at $61,439—51.3 percent below its October 6, 2025 peak of $126,080—with the Fear and Greed index at 11 [s554].

Across the feed, writers debated whether the drawdown reflects dollar-funding stress or structural exhaustion. The Bitcoin Zodiac observed that gold fell 9 percent, silver dropped 15 percent, and the Nasdaq lost more than 5 percent on Friday alongside bitcoin [s545]. Jeff Booth argued that bitcoin is forward-pricing an air gap in credit-backed asset valuations [s66], while moonsettler struck a starkly bearish tone on scaling and privacy [s9, s29]. Elsewhere, Halogen Capital targeted a December 2 listing on Bursa Malaysia for the country’s first spot bitcoin ETF [s547], and American Bitcoin secured a $150 million credit line from FalconX [s550].

Cryptography & Mining

Hardware Wallets Pass Post-Quantum Tests as Solo Miner Hits Block 323rd

Blockstream Research verified five hash-based signature schemes on existing signing devices, while an 11.1 TH/s home miner beat 1-in-1,650 odds.

Hardware wallets already in circulation can generate post-quantum signatures, according to Blockstream Research’s Q3 update [s257]. Engineers tested five hash-based schemes on four popular devices, including the Blockstream Jade Plus, and confirmed that all of them could sign [s257]. Separately, Blockstream reopened 2FA-protected 2-of-2 and 2-of-3 multisig account creation in its app [s369].

On the mining front, solo-pool operator Dr -ck congratulated miner bc1q~zy9j for solving the 323rd solo block on EU solo.ckpool.org with roughly 11.1 TH/s of total hashrate and a 3.47 TH/s worker—odds of about 1 in 1,650 over a year [s3].

Security & Patches

Bisq Issues Urgent Java4Shell Fix Ahead of Nov. 25 Cutoff

Reported by No Bullshit Bitcoin & Freedom.Tech

Peer-to-peer exchange Bisq released v2.1.16 (and v1.10.12 for Bisq 1) to update its bundled Java 21 runtime against Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) alongside the latest Tor security patch [s548, s96]. Release notes warn that "Updating to this version is required to continue trading," with a storage-format cutover set for November 25 [s548].

Freedom.Tech’s patch board also flagged same-day action on Tails 7.17.1 (an emergency uBlock Origin fix) and Frigate 0.18.3 (CVE-2026-123007, an unauthenticated root RCE), plus updates for Citrine 3.3.2, Jumble 26.11.2, and Core Lightning 26.12 [s539, s540]. Elsewhere, router maker GL.iNet published a November 20 security notice [s38].

Dispatches

Huddersfield Students Win Hackathon; Blackout Spurs Offline Ecash Plan

Computer science students from the University of Huddersfield—team Tibanna—won the hackathon with a tool that seals photos and videos with Nostr signatures and Bitcoin timestamps to prove provenance against AI fakes [s11].

In Peru, a seven-hour blackout in Ollantaytambo from 5:00 a.m. to noon gave developer Tim Bouma a live testbed for #ProjectOakgate, a planned app using local phone relays and NFC ecash that clears once mints reconnect [s284].

In corporate tech, Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and director, prompting lively reaction across the feed [s300, s15, s226].

Craft, Software & Field Notes

Oslo Workshop

Block-Height Knife Auction Survives Clock Glitch

By Gunnar Stødle

Knifemaker Gunnar Stødle closed a block-height auction at block 977,136 on nostrauction.shakespeare.wtf—and promptly ran into the rough edges of decentralized bidding [s265, s308]. Because of an nsite block-time lag, Stødle initially finalized the sale at 550k sats before spotting a 680k sat bid that had landed right at the closing block [s287, s340].

We ran strait into hidden comments, timestamp issues and vibecoded bug traps. he wrote, adding: Auctions are hard to get right, but man they are fun! [s308]. To thank the bidders and the auction app’s builder, Stødle offered each a production Cyberita Scandigrind knife free of charge [s308].

Personal Software

Tools Built for Four Users, Not Four Million

Dispatches from DrShift, ben, and Gutolx

Developer DrShift built Wichtelnest, a browser-based Secret Santa app on Nostr, so family members could draw names, build wishlists, and send anonymous gift messages without installing an app [s529]. Nothing groundbreaking, just a small side project that solved an actual problem for me. [s529].

That home-cooked ethos echoed across the day. Builder ben showed off a personal tide-tracker whose background wave rises and falls with the water level, free of logins [s247, s327]. And Gutolx highlighted a passage on small-scale software: One relay, one client, one key is a kitchen, not a failed restaurant. [s527].

Meanwhile, HiveTalk joined the monthly Bitcoin Shipshow as its official video conferencing partner [s531].

World & Sport

Caribbean Rail, Mossel Bay Ironman, and 2027 Runway

Traveler Leo filed a transit note from Santo Domingo, noting its two-line Metro—the Caribbean’s only subway—with an airport monorail on the way [s36].

In South Africa, BitcoinEkasi celebrated Akhona Mabuto finishing IRONMAN 70.3 Mossel Bay in 5:20:09, placing 14th of 202 in his age group—25 spots higher than 2025 [s114].

Finally, My First Bitcoin’s Impact Report showed the nonprofit is fully funded through 2026 with eight months of runway to July 2027, launching a 50/50 grassroots matching drive through December 31 [s40].
